o: Write the smallest program: make the robot move forward for 2 seconds and stop. Run it 5 times and record what happens.

questions.q: In "Kick-off circle Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write a one-page plan: task, parts or simulator, success rule, what could go wrong.
The mentor agrees the evidence you will produce in this module: a robot or simulator build log, a working program, 10 test runs and a safety note.
Set up the simulator or assemble the kit with a mentor. Check each wire, each moving part and each battery before power is on.
When it fails, change one thing only (a speed, a threshold, a sensor position) and run again. Keep every version.

questions.q: In "Build and first program Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Set up the simulator or assemble the kit with a mentor. Check each wire, each moving part and each battery before power is on.
Sensor averaging: three readings 12, 15 and 12 cm; average = 39/3 = 13 cm. One reading of 15 would have been 2 cm off.
Task: line-following robot, 2-metre line. 10 runs: 7 pass, 3 leave the line. Pass rate = 7/10 = 70%. Success rule was 80%.
Time cost: at 60% power a run took 8 s, at 45% it took 11 s. Time per run rose by 3 s, or 37.5% (3/8).

questions.q: In "Sensors, motors and safe operation Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Task: line-following robot, 2-metre line. 10 runs: 7 pass, 3 leave the line. Pass rate = 7/10 = 70%. Success rule was 80%.

When it fails, change one thing only (a speed, a threshold, a sensor position) and run again. Keep every version.
Motors: speed, torque, why wheels slip, why batteries sag, how to stop quickly and safely, why moving parts get a guard.

questions.q: In "Make it do the task Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Change one thing: lower speed from 60% to 45% power. 10 runs: 9 pass. Pass rate 90%.
Pick one task that is simple, safe and repeatable. Write the success rule in numbers (for example: follow a 2-metre line without leaving it, 8 times out of 10).
